title: trigger submission code is dead — keeper cannot actually fire triggers
description: runOnePollCycle imports buildTriggerTransaction and signAndSubmitTrigger but never calls them. After logging trigger_attempt, the body of the if-block is a comment that says 'In runOnePollCycle (test seam), we skip submission' — and the production main() loop calls runOnePollCycle as the only path, so submission is never wired up anywhere. From a simplicity lens this is the worst kind of accidental complexity: 184 LOC of triggerSubmitter.ts plus 5 imports in index.ts exist solely to be unused. The keeper cannot satisfy AC3.10 in this shape; the unused machinery should either be wired through (a single line: const { txDigest, triggerFired } = await signAndSubmitTrigger({...})) or the dead imports / dead module deleted.
impact: The 'simplicity envelope' question is moot because the code is also broken: ~190 LOC are dead, AC3.10 is unmet, and a future reader sees imports that imply a feature that does not exist. Cycle 5 will discover that the UI cannot drive the demo path.
recommendation: Either (a) delete the unused imports + the entire signAndSubmitTrigger function + buildTriggerTransaction if AC3.10 is descoped, or (b) wire submission inside the trigger-attempt branch of runOnePollCycle, gated on an injected signer arg so the test seam still works without keys. Option (b) is what the contract actually requires.
evidence:
// Note: trigger submission requires a signer, which is only available
    // in the full boot path. In runOnePollCycle (test seam), we skip submission.

title: deepCoinId and pollIntervalMs are accepted by runOnePollCycle but never used
description: PollCycleArgs declares deepCoinId and pollIntervalMs as required fields. The destructure at line 87 binds deepCoinId, but it is never referenced afterward; pollIntervalMs is never destructured at all. They appear in the type signature only because runOnePollCycle was supposed to call signAndSubmitTrigger (which needs deepCoinId). With trigger submission dead-coded (R4-001), these knobs are pure noise — every caller has to thread two arguments that have no effect.
impact: Misleads readers and tests about what the function does. The T-009 test must construct fake values for fields that affect nothing.
recommendation: Drop deepCoinId and pollIntervalMs from PollCycleArgs unless / until trigger submission is wired in. If kept, mark them at least as 'unused-pending-AC3.10-wiring'.
evidence: const { manifest, tpslVaultPackageId, deepCoinId, registry: externalRegistry } = args;

title: logger has 8 typed emitters that all delegate to one untyped emit — collapse
description: Six of the eight emitter functions (logVaultDiscovered, logPollCycle, logTriggerAttempt, logTriggerFired, logTriggerFailed, logPythReadFailed, logKeeperShutdown) are identical one-liners that call emit('info'|'warn', '<event_name>', args as unknown as Record<string, unknown>). The 'as unknown as Record<string, unknown>' cast appears 7 times — that is exactly the smell that says the type wrapper is buying nothing. Only logKeeperStarted does anything non-trivial (it destructures to drop unknown fields, which is also redundant with the SECRET_KEYS filter inside emit). 60+ LOC could collapse to a single typed `log(level, event, fields)` plus per-event TypeScript types declared near the call sites.
impact: Bloat: ~60 LOC for what one generic function does. Every new event name requires a new emitter, a new type, and a new test, with no actual safety gain (the cast erases the type).
recommendation: Replace the 8 emitters with one `log<E extends keyof EventMap>(level, event: E, fields: EventMap[E])`. Keep the SECRET_KEYS filter. Type safety improves and the file shrinks to ~40 LOC.
evidence: emit('info', 'vault_discovered', args as unknown as Record<string, unknown>);

title: BCS decoder hand-rolls u64 LE reads instead of using @mysten/sui/bcs
description: parsePriceFromBcs hand-implements readU64LE in a 6-line loop and indexes 5 manual offsets (0, 1, 9, 17, 18, 26). The file already imports `bcs` from '@mysten/sui/bcs' (used in buildGetPriceUnsafeTxKindB64). A simpler form would be a single bcs.struct({ priceNegative: bcs.bool(), priceMagnitude: bcs.u64(), conf: bcs.u64(), expoNegative: bcs.bool(), expoMagnitude: bcs.u64(), timestamp: bcs.u64() }).parse(bytes) — one declaration, no hand-counted offsets, decoder errors on length mismatch automatically. The contract explicitly references the SDK 2.x bcs API as preferred.
impact: Off-by-one risk in offsets if the layout ever changes; ~25 LOC of hand-rolled bit-shifting that the SDK already provides; future maintainer must re-derive the layout from bytes vs. reading the schema.
recommendation: Replace readU64LE + the manual offsets with `bcs.struct(...)` from @mysten/sui/bcs and call `.parse(bytes)`. The negative-price abort can wrap the parse result. notes/pyth-shape.md remains the canonical reference, but the code mirrors the layout declaratively.

title: shutdown handler sets `running = false` but immediately process.exit — flag is dead code
description: The shutdown handler does `running = false; logKeeperShutdown(...); process.exit(0);`. Because process.exit is synchronous and terminates the process before the next iteration of the while loop, the `running` boolean is never observed. The contract specified 'drain in-flight transactions' before exit — calling process.exit immediately defeats that. Either the boolean should actually gate the loop (drop process.exit, let the loop notice running=false at the next iteration boundary, then exit) or the boolean should be removed and the handler should just exit. As written, the pattern signals 'graceful shutdown' but provides none.
impact: Misleading code that implies a graceful-drain pattern that does not exist; an in-flight trigger submission (once wired per R4-001) would be killed mid-transaction.
recommendation: Drop the `running` flag and the while-loop guard, OR drop process.exit and let the loop see running=false at the next setTimeout resolve. Pick one shape; do not claim both.

title: void rpcUrl 'suppress unused warning' is a smell — rpcUrl was never needed in main()
description: main() reads `const rpcUrl = manifest.network.rpcUrl;` on line 301 and is never used; line 343 has `void rpcUrl; // suppress unused warning — used by runOnePollCycle via manifest`. The comment is a confession that the variable is dead. The fix is trivial — remove the binding entirely.
impact: One dead local + one comment that exists only to silence the compiler. Two-line subtraction.
recommendation: Delete the `const rpcUrl = manifest.network.rpcUrl` line and the corresponding `void rpcUrl;` line. Net: -2 LOC, +1 unit of clarity.
evidence: void rpcUrl; // suppress unused warning — used by runOnePollCycle via manifest

title: vaultRegistry has private console.warn JSON-build duplicating logger.ts shape
description: seedTriggeredFromChain hand-writes JSON.stringify({ ts: new Date().toISOString(), level: 'warn', event: 'seed_triggered_warning', vault_id, message }) directly to console.warn — twice. The keeper has a dedicated logger module (logger.ts) whose entire job is line-delimited JSON with this exact shape. Two costs: (a) the seed_triggered_warning event is a log line that is NOT typed in the logger, so AC3.11 contract drift is invisible; (b) the same shape is rebuilt by hand here — if the logger format changes, this drifts.
impact: Silent format drift between two emitters of the same kind of line; the registry now has an undeclared dependency on console.warn that bypasses the logger's secret-redaction.
recommendation: Add `logSeedTriggeredWarning(args)` to logger.ts and inject the logger (or import it). Removes ~16 LOC, ensures every log line goes through one path.

title: synthesis-notes claims eventType filter; code uses MoveModule filter
description: synthesis-notes.md line 24 says: '`eventType` filter used instead of `MoveModule` filter for `VaultCreated`'. The actual code at line 206 uses `{ MoveModule: { package: tpslVaultPackageId, module: 'tpsl_vault' } }`. This is fine on its own (the contract permits either), but the documentation drift is a simplicity smell — the synthesis notes are wrong and a reviewer trusting them would file the wrong finding. Either the filter should be MoveEventType (more precise per the contract) or the synthesis-notes should be corrected.
impact: Documentation/code mismatch propagates incorrect knowledge into FEEDBACK / RUNBOOK; no runtime defect today.
recommendation: Fix one or the other — preferably switch to MoveEventType, which is more precise and matches the synthesis claim. Cost: 4-line edit.

title: shouldFire check duplicates reason check (redundant guard)
description: `if (!evaluation.shouldFire || evaluation.reason === 'none' || evaluation.reason === 'already_triggered') continue;` — but evaluateTrigger's contract guarantees shouldFire=false IFF reason ∈ {'none','already_triggered'}. The reason-checks are tautological with !shouldFire. Either the type system says shouldFire=true ⇒ reason ∈ {'tp','sl'} and the cast on line 187 is safe (then drop the redundant reason checks), or it doesn't and the cast is unsafe. Either way the current shape is overdetermined.
impact: A reader wonders if there is a third case where shouldFire=true with reason='none'. There isn't, but the code suggests so.
recommendation: Replace with `if (!evaluation.shouldFire) continue;` and let TypeScript narrow reason to 'tp' | 'sl' via a discriminated-union shape on EvaluatorResult.

title: manifest module promised by contract was never created — inlined into index.ts as a TODO
description: Contract suggests `src/manifest.ts` to resolve vault `pool_id` to `(baseCoinType, quoteCoinType, baseDecimals, quoteDecimals, basePriceInfoObjectId, quotePriceInfoObjectId)`. That module does not exist. The resolution logic is inlined into runOnePollCycle with comments confessing the fact: 'Full manifest-driven mapping is handled in the manifest module.' (the module that doesn't exist) and `quoteDecimals: 9, // Default SUI decimals; manifest-driven in production`. The keeper hardcodes one pool's mapping (DEEP base + SUI quote) and silently produces wrong current_price for any other pool. The contract permits collapse but the inlined version produces wrong outputs for the SUI/USDC pool the manifest declares.
impact: The keeper cannot correctly fire triggers on the SUI/USDC pool the manifest declares because quoteDecimals is hardcoded to 9 and prices are hardcoded as DEEP/SUI. The module decomposition the contract suggested would have forced the implementer to confront this.
recommendation: Either implement src/manifest.ts as the contract suggested (with resolvePoolForVault returning the full tuple) and call it once per vault per tick, or document this deliberate scope cut. The hardcoded `quoteDecimals: 9` is a correctness bug in disguise — flag in design too.
evidence: quoteDecimals: 9, // Default SUI decimals; manifest-driven in production

title: VaultCreatedEventEnvelope has 8 fields, 7 of which are never read by the parser
description: VaultCreatedEventEnvelope declares { id, packageId, transactionModule, sender, type, parsedJson, bcs, timestampMs } but parseVaultCreatedEvent only reads `envelope.parsedJson`. The other seven fields exist purely to make discoverVaultsTick (in index.ts) build a complete envelope object that is then thrown away. This pushes complexity into the call site (index.ts lines 254-264 build the 8-field object from the raw RPC response) for zero benefit.
impact: ~30 LOC across two files exist to construct and type fields nobody reads. Any new RPC field requires updating the type even though parser doesn't care.
recommendation: Either change the parser signature to accept just `{ parsedJson: Record<string, unknown> }` (and drop the rest of the envelope type) or actually use the envelope fields for things like dedup-by-eventSeq.

title: registry.markTriggered / isTriggered / seedTriggeredFromChain unused in production code
description: VaultRegistry exposes seedTriggeredFromChain, markTriggered, and isTriggered. Production code (index.ts main() and runOnePollCycle) never calls any of them. They are exercised only by tests (T-002). Per contract Behavior step 3 of section 'Vault triggered ground-truth on restart' the keeper SHOULD seed triggered from chain at startup; that step is unimplemented. Per Behavior step 5 of the trigger loop the keeper MUST mark triggered after a successful fire — that is also missing (compounds R4-001).
impact: On restart, the keeper would attempt to re-fire already-triggered vaults (the contract's stated failure mode the seed call was supposed to prevent). Combined with R4-001, the vault doesn't get marked triggered after a fire either.
recommendation: Either remove the three methods (and document that the spec's recommended re-seed is descoped), or wire them into main() — the seed call in a loop after the first discovery tick, and markTriggered inside the trigger-success branch when R4-001 is fixed.
evidence: async seedTriggeredFromChain(vaultId: string, getObject: GetObjectFn): Promise<void> {

title: isMain detection logic is brittle and over-engineered for ESM entry point check
description: The 5-line isMain check builds an ad-hoc URL-vs-argv comparison: `import.meta.url.endsWith(process.argv[1].replace(/\\/g, '/'))`. The standard Node/ESM idiom is `import.meta.main` (Node 20.11+) or `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href === import.meta.url` from `node:url`. The current form silently breaks on Windows symlinks and on argv[1] containing query strings.
impact: Bug-class smell on Windows; the regex `/\\/g` partially anticipates this but doesn't cover all edge cases. More importantly: this logic is in the wrong file. A 3-line `bin/keeper.js` shim that imports and calls main() would remove the entire isMain block.
recommendation: Either use `import.meta.main` (Node ≥20.11) for the simplest 1-line check, or split main() into a separate `src/main.ts` entry point that just does `await main()` unconditionally. Drops 13 LOC.

title: synthesis-notes Transaction#serialize() deprecation note — the keeper does not call serialize at all
description: synthesis-notes flagged Transaction#serialize() deprecation. Searching the keeper source: serialize() is not called anywhere in src/ — only in the test file (tests/triggerSubmitter.test.ts uses it for structural inspection). So the deprecation does not affect production. The simplicity finding is on the test side: T-006 binds to `Transaction.serialize()` which the SDK has marked deprecated. Migrating tests to `tx.getData()` (the SDK 2.x replacement) future-proofs T-006 without touching production code.
impact: No production impact; tests will start emitting deprecation warnings on every run as the SDK matures.
recommendation: Migrate the T-006 test from tx.serialize() to tx.getData() per the SDK 2.0 docs. Production source needs no change.
evidence: asserts on the structural shape — NOT on internal SDK encoding bytes.

title: manifest interface duplicates SandboxManifest types that should live in a manifest module
description: SandboxManifest, the four package fields, the pyth oracle pair, and the pools record are inline-declared in index.ts and re-derived ad hoc in runOnePollCycle (manifest.packages.pyth?.packageId ?? '', manifest.pythOracles.deepPriceInfoObjectId, etc.). Compounds R4-010 — the contract suggested src/manifest.ts to own this type plus the pool resolution. As-is, the manifest type is the second-largest type in the codebase and it lives in the file with the longest function. Splitting it out (mirroring the contract's suggestion) makes index.ts ~30 LOC shorter and gives the SUI/USDC pool resolution a home.
impact: index.ts is 359 LOC — the largest module in the keeper. Most of the bloat is two concerns living together: the entry point AND the manifest schema AND the discovery helper AND runOnePollCycle. Decomposition would cleanly halve it.
recommendation: Move SandboxManifest to a new src/manifest.ts (typed loadManifest(path) plus resolvePoolForVault). Keep index.ts focused on boot + lifecycle. Net: same LOC overall, better separation, the SUI/USDC pool gets handled correctly.
